_meta: SAMPLE agent outputs for the agency dashboard demo. Written by hand to show what each agent produces; not from live model runs. Numbers marked 'computed' in dashboard/data/demo.json come from the real rules code instead.

onboarding.summary: Two friends from San Francisco want a relaxed week across Lisbon and Barcelona in mid-November: food markets, architecture, live music, one day trip. Flights and stays are already booked; they want help with everything around them.

captured.label: Travelers
captured.value: Maya Chen (US passport), Arjun Rao (Indian passport, US green card)

advisor_notes: Arjun mentioned a Schengen visa appointment but wasn't sure of the date.
Maya 'thinks' her passport is fine. Worth checking.
They'd like one person to call if anything goes wrong on the trip.

planning.title: Plan & Book
planning.tagline: From idea to a bookable trip

runs.headline: Itinerary assembled; one passport problem found
runs.summary: Imported the 3 flights, 2 stays and 3 reservations into one itinerary. Checked entry rules for both travelers: Arjun's Schengen visa appointment is booked for Nov 5. Maya's passport expires Jan 30, 2027, which is less than the 3 months Schengen requires after leaving on Nov 21.

documents.detail: Expires 2027-01-30. Schengen needs validity until at least 2027-02-21. Expedited renewal required before Nov 12.
Appointment Nov 5, 10:30 at the Consulate General of Spain, San Francisco.

actions.summary: Tell Maya she needs an expedited passport renewal
actions.draft: Hi Maya, your passport expires on Jan 30, 2027. For Portugal and Spain it needs to be valid for 3 months after you leave the Schengen area (until at least Feb 21, 2027). Please book an expedited renewal this week; we can send you the appointment links.

handoffs.task: Brief both travelers for PT + ES, Nov 12–21

runs.headline: Packing lists ready for mild days, cool evenings
runs.summary: Built a list per traveler around one checked bag each (23 kg) and a carry-on. November climate averages: Lisbon about 18°C by day and 12°C at night, Barcelona about 17°C and 10°C, with a few rainy days.

runs.headline: 48-hour kit for Arjun's delayed bag
runs.summary: Recovery asked for an overnight kit near Hotel Jardí de Gràcia. Suggested a pharmacy and a basics store within a 10-minute walk, open until 21:00 (mock store data). Keep every receipt: the airline owes reasonable interim costs.

explore.title: Explore & Experience
explore.tagline: Make the most of every day

runs.headline: 3 reservations confirmed, vegetarian-friendly
runs.summary: Booked around their pace: one day trip, one dinner on arrival in Barcelona, and timed entry for Sagrada Família on a morning with nothing else planned.

runs.headline: Dinner still works with the delay
runs.summary: With the new 17:05 arrival, the 20:30 tapas dinner in Gràcia still leaves 3 hours for the airport transfer and hotel check-in. Kept the booking. Magic found two low-effort ideas for the gap before dinner.

magic.title: Sunset at Bunkers del Carmel
magic.why: Best city view, 25 min from Gràcia by bus + short walk

magic.title: Vermouth in Plaça del Sol
magic.why: Two minutes from the hotel; easy if they're tired

runs.headline: Pre-departure briefing for Portugal and Spain
runs.summary: Both countries use the euro, Type F plugs at 230V, and 112 for emergencies. Cards work almost everywhere; keep some cash for small cafés and markets. No travel insurance yet: recommended a policy with medical, trip-delay and baggage-delay cover.

items: Pay in euros, not dollars, when a card terminal offers a choice
Keep about €50 cash each for markets and small cafés
Tipping isn't expected; round up for good service
One Europe eSIM covers both countries
Install before the flight; turn on at landing
Tap water is safe in both cities
Watch for pickpockets on Lisbon tram 28 and Barcelona's La Rambla
Buy before Nov 8: medical, trip delay, and baggage delay cover
Arjun: check that the policy covers non-US passport holders

actions.summary: Send travel-insurance options to both travelers
actions.draft: We recommend a policy with medical, trip-delay and baggage-delay cover before Nov 8. Here are three options to compare (links in the app).

recovery.title: Manage & Recover
recovery.tagline: Handle what doesn't go to plan

runs.headline: VY8461 delayed 4h10m: EUR 500 claim ready
runs.summary: The Lisbon → Barcelona flight now lands at 17:05 instead of 12:55. The cause is technical, so the airline owes compensation. Both travelers are also entitled to meals and refreshments at the airport. No rebooking needed.

actions.summary: Send EU261 claim to Vueling for 2 passengers
actions.draft: Booking VL93TR, flight VY8461 LIS-BCN on 17 Nov 2026. The flight arrived 250 minutes late for a technical reason. Under Regulation (EC) 261/2004 we claim EUR 250 per passenger for Maya Chen and Arjun Rao (EUR 500 total). Please pay to the card used for the booking.

runs.headline: Arjun's bag didn't arrive
runs.summary: Report filed at the airport (PIR BCNVY10293); delivery expected Nov 19. Arjun can buy essentials now and claim them back. The written claim is due within 21 days of getting the bag.

runs.headline: Receipt logged: €38.40, claimable
runs.summary: Farmàcia Gràcia receipt recorded against the bag incident and marked claimable. It will go into the baggage claim.

runs.headline: Trip closed: settle-up and follow-ups
runs.summary: Everyone's home. Expenses are reconciled in USD, and three follow-ups are on the list: the EU261 claim, the baggage claim, and the welcome-home tasks.

actions.draft: PIR BCNVY10293, flight VY8461, 17 Nov 2026. Bag delivered 19 Nov. Claiming EUR 38.40 for essentials bought while it was delayed; receipt attached.

tasks: Follow up on the EU261 claim if there's no reply by Dec 22
Submit the baggage claim by Dec 10 (21 days after delivery)
Restart mail delivery and check on the plants
